author: Frosty
text:
What I have found and learned about CPs are as follows: - Upward-sloping CP to a supply zone = price more likely to go down from the supply zone (provided the last demand in CP PAZ is engulfed down)

- Downward-sloping CP from a supply zone = price more likely to go up through the supply zone (provided there is an engulf up of the last supply in CP PAZ and the last demand after CP holds price up)

- Downward-sloping CP to a demand zone = price more likely to go up from the demand zone (provided the last supply in CP PAZ is engulfed up)

- Upward-sloping CP from a demand zone = price more likely to go down through the demand zone (provided there is an engulf down of the last demand in CP PAZ and the last supply after CP holds price down)

- CP followed by LQ without engulf of the approach flag = potential bounce later on from base of LQ - CP that didn't activate immediately, i.e. price didn't engulf the last approach flag in the CP, will still be effective at a later date - The best way to trade a CP is to let price engulf the last approach flag, i.e. the last demand or supply in the CP PAZ, and enter on a RT to a previous DP - If price engulfs the last approach flag in the CP PAZ, then price will slide through to the base of CP PAZ - CP can be used by ITs to push price in the direction of a DP if there is not enough order to reach the DP (easier to explain with a charthere)

- CP away from a demand or a supply level can be used later on to create LQ spikes that could trap retail traders into selling or buying into a demand or supply level, respectively, for the ITs to fill in opposite orders (seehere for example)

Please correct any incorrect interpretations of CPThank you all for your comments and criticism P. S. Sorry for double posting this also on the CP homework since I think this is very important for my understanding of the subject and should also belong in the journal

Hi everyone, As bro Staurum pointed out, I should start understanding FTRs first before touching FLs. This will be my first homework on FTRs.

I've been reading the FTR thread and Les_Paul's journal before doing this homework. I'll post below on what I have learned from those threads. As usual, please correct any inaccurate statements Also from now on, I will do all the other homeworks here for easier reference to check my progress and any other conceptual enlightenment that all of you share to me. I also don't want to clutter this precious website with my noob level homeworks Please criticize and comment on this homework as I believe this and PAZs are the most vital concepts that RTM students should understand What I have learned on FTRs and PAZs: 1. FTRs are created on the deepest retrace after a break of important high and low, a break of FTR created in the opposite swing, a break of pre-CP, or a break of base of CP. 2. The best way to trade FTRs is to wait for an engulf of an FTR in the opposite direction and enter on a retrace to the source of the engulf, which most of the time is inside another FTR 3. There are a few types of PAZ: CP PAZ, Stacked SD PAZ, the space between 2 FTRs 4. True engulfs are those that engulfs FTRs. Some engulfs are fake engulfs to trick retail traders into taking opposite orders that the ITs want to trade against. This fake engulf (FO), usually stops at the FTR, where the ITs' orders lie 5. Engulf of an FTR, price wants to go to the next FTR in the direction of the engulf Questions that I have not yet found the answer to: 1. I don't understand why price stopped at a minor FTR instead of the blue box (I circled my question in blue oval). Any hints on this?

2. The space between the two FTRs: FTR A and B, is this the FO zone?

author: Frosty

From studying the chart again a few more times and your guidance, I think that FTR A is very important because it is the LS kink and it is also a price reversal FTR, which is the first FTR that is created after an engulf of a series of higher FTRs.

After breaking down from the LS kink area, price then creates an FTR, which is the important one where price bounced later on. I'm guessing from reading the FL thread a while back, we call this FTR the mouth of the FL.

The blue box is also an FTR but it is made from a break of a local FTR not obvious in the higher TF, i.e. weekly chart.
